scope: Paired-rectangle certificates for three count-aware final-MAD families. The h bypass is one T instruction over eight stated initial words/root-only constants. Numerator/count may be arbitrary T-only expressions; there is exactly one SHR and no other non-T operation. Only q*count+h, count*h+q and q*h+count are covered. Fixed allowed root0x12345678; no full four-op or kernel lower bound.
proof: On an eight-point b16..18 fibre the target low3 is a permutation, while all T-prefix low3 words are fixed. Hence q low3 must distinguish all eight points, so at most one count can clamp to0. On every other point actual count equals one common c in16..23, by low16 invariance and the universal count band. The two disjoint four-point rectangles cover the fibre, so at least one is entirely unclamped. Both have Delta(h)=0 for every root parameter and target mixed distance greater than3014610. But q*c+h has mixed distance at most2*c*65535, and c*h+q has at most2*65535, contradictions on that unclamped rectangle. For q*h+count, the separate complete low-half inverse scan proves neither rectangle pair can satisfy the product equations; target low16 avoids the count band, so no clamped point is possible in this third family.
